companies.name: TRUMPF SE + Co. KG
companies.role: The CO2 drive laser that ignites the plasma inside every EUV lithography machine
companies.description: TRUMPF is a family-owned German machine-tool and laser company that builds the only laser on Earth capable of driving an EUV light source. In five amplifier stages it boosts a CO2 seed pulse of a few watts more than 10,000 times to over 30 kilowatts of mean power, then fires it twice at each of 50,000 tin droplets per second. The finished laser weighs more than 10 tonnes and contains around 450,000 individual parts, and there is no second supplier: ASML's EUV roadmap is gated by TRUMPF's amplifier roadmap. In 2025 ASML gave TRUMPF its Technology supplier award for 'first light' from a next-generation high-energy EUV laser.

companies.name: Carl Zeiss SMT GmbH
companies.role: EUV projection optics — the mirrors that focus 13.5 nm light onto the wafer
companies.description: ZEISS Semiconductor Manufacturing Technology, based in Oberkochen, makes the illumination and projection optics for every ASML EUV scanner. EUV light is absorbed by glass and by air, so the pattern is steered entirely by mirrors coated with 100+ alternating molybdenum/silicon layers a few nanometres thick and polished to roughly 50 picometres RMS — less than one atom of roughness. ZEISS's own comparison: scale one of these mirrors up to the size of Germany and the tallest bump on it would still be under a millimetre. ASML has no alternative supplier, and ZEISS is a co-investor in ASML's High-NA EUV programme.

companies.name: Cymer LLC (ASML San Diego)
companies.role: Light sources for lithography: DUV excimer lasers and the EUV laser-produced-plasma source
companies.description: Founded in 1986 by two college friends in San Diego and acquired by ASML in 2013, Cymer built the excimer laser light sources (ArF and KrF) that made deep-ultraviolet lithography an industry. The same San Diego site now designs, qualifies and builds ASML's EUV laser-produced-plasma source, including the droplet generator that fires 50,000 molten tin droplets a second into the path of TRUMPF's CO2 laser, flashing each into a ~220,000 C plasma that radiates 13.5 nm light. ASML bought the company precisely because the light source was the single hardest bottleneck on the EUV roadmap.

companies.name: VDL Enabling Technologies Group (VDL ETG)
companies.role: Dutch contract manufacturer of the modules, frames and vacuum vessels inside ASML machines
companies.description: VDL ETG is the mechatronics arm of the family-owned Dutch VDL Groep and one of ASML's largest single suppliers. It co-engineers and builds complete modules rather than parts: the vacuum vessel that houses the EUV source with its cabling, wafer handlers, and the ultra-stiff frames that hold ZEISS's mirrors in position inside next-generation EUV machines. This is the invisible middle layer of the supply chain — a Brabant machine shop grown into a systems integrator that only exists because ASML sits 10 km away.

companies.name: ASML Holding N.V.
companies.role: The only maker of EUV lithography machines — the tools that print leading-edge chip patterns
companies.description: Spun out of a 1984 Philips joint venture in Veldhoven, ASML is the sole company able to build the TWINSCAN NXE:3800E, the EUV scanner behind every 2 nm-class logic and leading-edge DRAM process. One machine pulls together roughly 5,000 suppliers: TRUMPF's CO2 laser, ZEISS's atomically smooth mirrors, VDL's frames, vacuum pumps that remove atoms one at a time. The finished tool is too large to ship assembled — it goes out in roughly 250 crates aboard three Boeing 747s plus 40 freight containers and a small army of engineers who spend weeks rebuilding it on the fab floor. ASML is also one of the few non-American companies subject to US export controls.

companies.name: Applied Materials, Inc.
companies.role: Deposition, ion implantation, CMP and metrology — most of the non-lithography toolset
companies.description: Applied Materials is the broadest equipment maker in the industry and the one almost nobody outside the fab has heard of. It supplies the deposition tools that lay down metal and insulator films an atom at a time, the ion implanters that literally put the 'semi' in semiconductor, the chemical-mechanical polishers that flatten each layer back down, and the metrology tools that check the previous steps worked. Its share of some of these niches is extreme — around 60%+ of CMP and roughly half of ion implantation — and without a fab full of Applied tools, even an ASML EUV scanner is a very expensive laser pointer.

companies.name: Lam Research Corporation
companies.role: Plasma etch — carving the lithographer's pattern into the actual silicon
companies.description: Lam Research dominates plasma etch, the step where the pattern a scanner projects in photoresist is actually cut into the wafer. Its Kiyo conductor-etch and Flex dielectric-etch modules, now on the compact Sense.i platform, are the reference tools for high-aspect-ratio features — the deep, near-vertical holes that make 3D NAND stacks and DRAM capacitors possible. Lam also supplies electrochemical deposition and photoresist strip/clean, so a single wafer can pass through its tools dozens of times. Its 2025 Akara conductor etch system added cryogenic etching and automated maintenance.

companies.name: KLA Corporation
companies.role: Wafer and reticle inspection plus process control — the fab's very expensive microscopes
companies.description: KLA makes most of the world's inspection and metrology equipment: the optical and e-beam systems that hunt for nanometre-scale defects on wafers, reticles and mask blanks and tell a fab whether what it just built is any good before millions of dollars of wafers get scrapped. Its Surfscan line dates back to 1984 and the Puma, Voyager and eS-series families remain the de facto standard for leading-edge yield management. KLA holds roughly 55-60% of the whole process-control market, a bigger share of its category than any other member of the 'big five'.

companies.name: Tokyo Electron Limited (TEL)
companies.role: Coater/developer tracks that bracket every lithography step, plus thermal processing and cleaning
companies.description: Tokyo Electron holds one of the quietest near-monopolies in the industry: roughly 90% of the global coater/developer market and effectively 100% of the tracks used with EUV. Its CLEAN TRACK LITHIUS platform coats each wafer with photoresist, hands it to the scanner and develops it afterwards, so no wafer reaches an ASML machine without passing through a TEL tool first — over 3,000 LITHIUS Pro systems have shipped. TEL also holds strong positions in thermal processing, single-wafer cleaning, etch and wafer bonding, which is why it sits in the 'big five' alongside far more famous names.

companies.name: Nikon Corporation
companies.role: ArF immersion scanners and i-line steppers for mature and mid-tier nodes
companies.description: Yes, the camera company — Nikon is one of only two firms besides ASML that still builds semiconductor lithography systems, and with ASML the only other maker of ArF immersion scanners, though ASML holds roughly 90% of that market. Its line runs from the NSR-S636E immersion scanner down to the NSR-2205iL1 i-line stepper: a generation behind on resolution, with no EUV product at all. That matters less than it sounds, because most chips made today go into routers, washing machines and cars, and a Nikon tool skips the US export-control paperwork entirely. Intel was long its anchor customer; Nikon is now pushing into Korea, China and Southeast Asia.

companies.name: Canon Inc.
companies.role: i-line and KrF steppers for mature nodes, plus nanoimprint lithography
companies.description: The other camera maker in the lithography business, Canon dominates the unglamorous end of the market with roughly 80% of i-line lithography and around 233 systems shipped in 2024 — about 30% of all lithography units sold worldwide, making it number two by volume even though it sells nothing near the leading edge. In 2023 it launched the FPA-1200NZ2C, the world's first commercial nanoimprint lithography tool, which stamps circuit patterns onto wafers instead of projecting them, and in July 2025 it opened its first new lithography factory in 21 years at Utsunomiya. For any fab that does not strictly need EUV, a Canon tool is cheaper and skips the diplomatic paperwork.
